title: Meat — Composition, Types, Slaughtering, Tenderisation and Curing
shortDescription: Muscle structure, post-mortem changes, slaughter steps, tenderisation and curing chemistry.
genZNote: Meat science is a plot of glycogen, pH and time. Rigor mortis → ageing → tender meat — don't skip the waiting period.

sections.heading: Composition and Types
bullets: Lean meat: water ~70–75%, protein ~19–22%, fat variable (1–20%+), ash ~1%; muscle proteins: myofibrillar (actin, myosin), sarcoplasmic (myoglobin), stromal (collagen, elastin).
Types: beef/carabeef (cattle/buffalo), mutton (sheep), chevon (goat), pork, poultry, game; red vs white meat depends on myoglobin.
Meat inspection (ante- and post-mortem) and hygienic slaughter in licensed slaughterhouses; rules under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001 and FSS regulations.

steps.name: Pre-slaughter rest and ante-mortem inspection
steps.explanation: Rest and water reduce stress and glycogen loss.

steps.name: Stunning and bleeding
steps.explanation: Rapid humane stunning followed by sticking and bleeding.

steps.name: Dressing, evisceration, inspection, chilling
steps.explanation: Skinning, removing offal, carcass wash, chill to ≤ 4 °C.

steps.name: Rigor mortis
steps.explanation: Glycogen → lactic acid; pH falls from ~7 to 5.4–5.6; ATP depletion locks actin–myosin.

steps.name: Ageing/conditioning
steps.explanation: Hold at 0–4 °C (beef 7–14 days) so endogenous proteases (calpains, cathepsins) tenderise.

sections.heading: Tenderisation and Curing
bullets: Tenderisation: ageing, enzymes (papain, bromelain, ficin), mechanical (pounding, blade tenderisation), electrical stimulation, calcium chloride injection, marinating in acid.
Quality defects: PSE (pale, soft, exudative) pork from rapid pH drop at high temperature; DFD (dark, firm, dry) beef from low glycogen.

Curing: salt, nitrite/nitrate, sugar, ascorbate/erythorbate and phosphates; nitrite forms nitrosomyoglobin (pink) and inhibits Clostridium botulinum; methods: dry, wet (brine), injection; smoking adds flavour and antimicrobial action.
Residual nitrite is regulated; nitrosamine formation is a concern.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Meat quality depends on muscle composition, hygienic slaughter, post-mortem pH decline and subsequent conditioning, tenderisation and curing.
keyFacts: PSE in pork; DFD in beef.
Nitrite fixes colour and inhibits C. botulinum.

commonTraps: Do not cook or cut meat in pre-rigor and expect tenderness.

sources.name: Hui: Handbook of Food Science, Technology and Engineering
